messages:
maya: Heads-up — we're seeing sustained egress saturation from dedicated-pool-3 (eu-west-2). Packet drops and long tail latencies for internal RPCs + model downloads.
samir: Confirmed. Network metrics show NIC at 98% for several hosts. tracert shows retries, tail latency spikes on GPU jobs. :facepalm: 
jin: Any recent deploys to that pool? Could be a new training job pulling checkpoints.
maya: No deploys. Most heavy tenants are inference-only, but one team spun up a large shard sync yesterday.
kate: Upload of large KV caches + model shards in parallel. If that's saturating the egress, noisy neighbor effect for other tenants is expected.
luis: Can we throttle at the host/tenant level? We've been relying on soft isolation via cgroups only for compute, not for NIC egress.
samir: We could apply tc qdisc tbf/htb per veth, but scale is painful. eBPF-based policies would be better for per-tenant shaping.
jin: Quick mitigation: move the heavy tenant to a dedicated-sparse pool and limit their burst credits. That avoids touching critical infra.
maya: Agreed — I'll patch the scheduler to prefer dedicated-pool-burst for that tenant and evict non-critical jobs. Doing it now.
ops-bot: Alert created: INC-2026-1298 — Egress saturation on dedicated-pool-3. Pager duty paged.
maya: Immediate relief after moving 3 pods to dedicated-sparse — NIC back to ~60% on previous hosts.
samir: Can we instrument per-tenant egress accounting? Right now we only have host-level bits in Prometheus.
kate: We have flow logs in the VPC but parsing is slow. Proposal: export sampled sFlow to our pipeline and tag by tenant ID at CNI layer.
luis: Long-term, SR-IOV or NIC partitioning could give strong isolation but adds provisioning complexity and cost.
jin: Another option: enforce model shard rate limits in the runtime — stagger KV downloads and backoff aggressively.
maya: Runtime change would help; need to coordinate with eng-runtime. How risky is a backoff change? Any perf regressions?
jin: Low risk if opt-in per tenant. We'll add a token-bucket for shard fetches: allow burst then slow steady refill.
samir: Cost question: dedicated pools for heavy tenants increases spend. Need to quantify delta: burst-friendly versus shared with egress shaping.
luis: I'll run a cost model: dedicated-pool baseline + extra NICs vs shared + engineering time to build eBPF shaper.
maya: Ops action items: 1) Move heavy tenant to dedicated-sparse (done) 2) Short-term: apply tc rate limit on remaining hot nodes for that tenant 3) Medium: enable per-tenant egress accounting 4) Long-term: runtime fetch backoff + SR-IOV evaluation.
kate: I'm adding a short circuit in scheduler: if tenant egress > 80% of NIC for >5m, auto-migrate to sparse-dedicated.
samir: Can you post the iftop snippet you captured? Might help SRE tuning.
kate: Putting snippet:
```
eth0: 950Mb/s TX 980Mb/s RX
Top flows:
10.0.1.23:80 -> 10.0.2.5:443  380Mb/s  (tenant: search-prod)
10.0.1.23:80 -> 10.0.2.9:443  320Mb/s  (tenant: kv-sync)
```
maya: Also saw tcp retransmits jump on host: netstat -s | grep retransmits -> 1200 in 10m.
jin: For the tc approach, sample commands if we need quick band-aid:
```
# limit to 400mbit on veth123
tc qdisc replace dev veth123 root tbf rate 400mbit burst 32kb latency 50ms
```
luis: Remember this is per-host; with ephemeral veths created by CNI, need mapping tenant->veth. That mapping is the hard bit.
samir: eBPF hooks at CNI level can annotate skb with tenant ID and enforce shaping without per-veth config. Worth prototyping.
kate: I'll open a design doc for eBPF shaper and link to INC-2026-1298. Also adding scheduler rule PR to repo.
maya: Thanks — for now monitoring shows much better tail latencies. Keeping this thread open until tomorrow 09:00 UTC to confirm stability.
deploy-bot: Scheduled migration completed for tenant search-prod -> dedicated-sparse-2 at 2026-03-17T22:46:10Z :rocket: 
samir: Re-checking metrics now — 95th latency down 3x. Solid.
luis: Cost estimation queued, ETA end of day.
maya: Great work. If anyone sees recurrence, ping here with pcap or iftop output. :thumbsup:
